newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor shares rise on 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Accor shares rise on 1996 sales.

text.p: Shares in French hotel group Accor rose on Wednesday as traders focused on an increase in its 1996 sales on a like-for-like basis rather than on the overall drop.

Traders said the share was also benefiting from a view that the hotel industry appeared to be recovering, helped by the dollar's gain and other currency shifts. It was up 1.96 percent at 779 francs at 1428 GMT.

The group's 1996 sales fell to 28.31 billion francs from 31.01 billion. However, excluding Eurest, sold to Compass in October 1995, sales were up 8.3 percent. At constant structure and currencies, they were up 2.5 percent.

"We're staying positive because we think we're seeing a recovery in the hotel industry cycle in continental Europe and Accor, which has been very exposed, will be the first share in the sector to benefit," said Jean-Jacques Vironda, an analyst at Societe Generale.
Another analyst said the outlook was bright. "Occupancy rates are rising. We should also see the average price (per room) increase. This situation should help generate profits," he said.
